2609.28565.title: When Explanations Cannot Be Read: Measuring and Correcting SHAP and LIME Rendering for Right-to-Left Languages
2609.28565.paper_summary: Post hoc explanation methods such as SHAP and LIME are widely used to interpret text classifiers, but their visualizations are mainly designed for left-to-right languages. When applied to right-to-left (RTL) languages such as Urdu, Arabic, Persian, and Hebrew, the attribution values remain mathematically valid, while their visual presentation fails. Tokens appear out of sequence, connected letterforms break apart, and plot layouts do not follow the natural reading direction. This study addresses this gap as a visualization problem rather than a limitation of the explanation methods themselves. We present SHAP-RTL, a rendering layer that corrects reading direction and script shaping in SHAP and LIME visualizations, with per-language font selection, while preserving the original attribution values, feature ordering, and model outputs. The approach is evaluated on Urdu, Arabic, Hebrew, and Persian hate and offensive-language datasets using TF-IDF and logistic regression classifiers. Rendering correctness is measured by an OCR round trip over 200 feature words per language. Default rendering yields character error rates of 0.820 to 0.979, meaning the label no longer carries its token; the common reshape-and-reorder workaround fails for Urdu at 0.998, worse than no correction; and the Matplotlib 3.11.0 text rewrite inverts that workaround, while SHAP-RTL remains correct under both versions. The framework also verbalizes the same attributions as short contextual explanations in the reader's language, constrained to the identified features. Evaluation in this paper concerns rendering correctness; assessment of the generated explanations is left to future work. The study highlights the importance of language-aware visualization in making post hoc explainability more accessible across different writing systems.
2609.28565.paper_summary_zh: 後 hoc 解釋方法如 SHAP 和 LIME 被廣泛用於解釋文本分類器，但其視覺化主要設計用於從左到右的語言。當應用於從右到左（RTL）語言如烏爾都語、阿拉伯語、波斯語和希伯來語時，歸因值在數學上仍然有效，但其視覺呈現卻失敗。標記出現順序錯誤，連接的字母形狀分開，圖表佈局未遵循自然閱讀方向。本研究將這一差距視為視覺化問題，而非解釋方法本身的限制。我們提出了 SHAP-RTL，一個渲染層，修正了 SHAP 和 LIME 視覺化中的閱讀方向和字形，並根據每種語言選擇字體，同時保留原始的歸因值、特徵排序和模型輸出。該方法在烏爾都語、阿拉伯語、希伯來語和波斯語的仇恨和攻擊性語言數據集上進行評估，使用 TF-IDF 和邏輯回歸分類器。渲染正確性通過每種語言的 200 個特徵詞進行 OCR 回合測量。默認渲染的字符錯誤率為 0.820 到 0.979，這意味著標籤不再攜帶其標記；對於烏爾都語，常見的重塑和重新排序的變通方法失敗，達到 0.998，甚至比不進行修正還要糟糕；而 Matplotlib 3.11.0 的文本重寫則反轉了該變通方法，而 SHAP-RTL 在兩個版本下均保持正確。該框架還將相同的歸因以讀者的語言表達為簡短的上下文解釋，並限制於已識別的特徵。本文的評估關注渲染正確性；對生成解釋的評估留待未來的工作。該研究突顯了語言感知視覺化在使後 hoc 可解釋性在不同書寫系統中更具可及性的重要性。
